callouts.label: Notice Body Signals
callouts.hint: The student at far left pausing with one hand near the chest.
callouts.description: A nervous stomach, tight muscles, or a strong urge to leave can be useful information.
callouts.tip: A student never needs perfect proof before moving toward safety.

callouts.label: Recognize Peer Pressure
callouts.hint: The small peer group talking on the left-side path.
callouts.description: Peer pressure can be direct or as subtle as “everyone else is doing it.”
callouts.tip: Ask whether the choice is safe, kind, and consistent with your values.

callouts.label: Spot a Trusted Helper
callouts.hint: The open school office where an adult is listening.
callouts.description: Knowing where trusted people are is part of calm situational awareness.
callouts.tip: A teacher, counselor, coach, family member, or other established trusted adult can help.

callouts.label: Keep a Public Way Out
callouts.hint: The broad, open path through the center of the scene.
callouts.description: Notice exits and well-used public routes before you need them.
callouts.tip: Situational awareness is a calm scanning habit, not constant fear.

callouts.label: Use a Direct No
callouts.hint: The student in purple using a calm stop-hand gesture.
callouts.description: A short, clear refusal can be enough: “No thanks, I’m not doing that.”
callouts.tip: A refusal does not require an apology or debate.

callouts.label: Suggest Something Safer
callouts.hint: The student in green offering another idea with open hands.
callouts.description: An alternative can redirect a group toward a safe or kind activity.
callouts.tip: If pressure continues, stop negotiating and leave.

callouts.label: Move Toward Safe People
callouts.hint: The bright community-center entrance in the upper right.
callouts.description: Choose a public place with safe people rather than becoming isolated.
callouts.tip: Getting distance is more important than winning an argument.

callouts.label: Contact a Trusted Adult
callouts.hint: The student using a phone on the right-side path.
callouts.description: Call or message an established trusted adult and explain where you are.
callouts.tip: If it is an emergency, get immediate help through the appropriate local emergency service.

callouts.label: Tell What Happened
callouts.hint: The seated adult listening carefully near the home.
callouts.description: Tell a trusted adult even if the situation ended or you are unsure how serious it was.
callouts.tip: “Something felt wrong” is enough to begin.

callouts.label: Reach a Safe Destination
callouts.hint: The well-lit home doorway at the far right.
callouts.description: A practiced route ends with safety and support, not with handling everything alone.
callouts.tip: Review what helped so the plan is easier to use next time.
